facts.label: Egypt
facts.fact: In the Egyptian judgment the jackal-headed Anubis steadies the scales as the heart is weighed against truth.

facts.label: Babylon & Sumer
facts.fact: The inlaid Standard of Ur gives a vivid picture of Early Dynastic kingship and its beliefs about the beyond.

facts.label: Assyria
facts.fact: Mesopotamia's great underworld poem is the Descent of Inanna, in which even a goddess is stripped at each gate.

facts.label: The Indus
facts.fact: Mohenjo-daro's most striking structure is the Great Bath, a watertight sunken tank of fitted brick sealed with bitumen.

facts.label: Greece
facts.fact: Greek myth tells of Persephone carried off to the underworld, sought by Demeter and returned for part of the year.

facts.label: Persia
facts.fact: At Behistun, Darius carved his victories into living rock and credited Ahura Mazda — a landmark royal inscription.

facts.label: Bactria
facts.fact: Zoroastrians exposed their dead on the dakhmas, the Towers of Silence, so the sun and vultures might strip the bones.

facts.label: China
facts.fact: The Zhou justified conquering the Shang by the Mandate of Heaven — a ruler holds power only while he rules justly.

facts.label: Rome
facts.fact: On the summit stood the Capitoline Triad — Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva — guarantors of Roman power.

facts.label: Canaan
facts.fact: The clay tablets of Ugarit lay bare a Canaanite pantheon — El the father, Baal the storm-rider, Asherah the mother — the older world the Bible set itself against.

facts.label: Hatti
facts.fact: The Hittites crowned a storm-god, Tarhunna, matched to the Hurrian Teshub — striding on a bull with the lightning in his fist.
